messages.content: What are the components of Civil Law?

message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Legal Sources** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Judicial Precedent** – Decisions from higher courts that guide lower courts.
• **Customary Law** – Long‑standing practices recognized as binding. | | **Core Areas of Law** | • **Contract Law** – Rules governing agreements, obligations, and remedies for breach.
• **Tort Law** – Liability for wrongful acts causing harm or loss.
• **Property Law** – Rights and duties related to real and personal property.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody, adoption.
• **Inheritance Law** – Distribution of estates after death.
• **Commercial Law** – Business transactions, company formation, bankruptcy. | | **Procedural Elements** | • **Civil Procedure Rules** – Guidelines for filing claims, evidence, discovery, and trial conduct.
• **Jurisdiction & Venue** – Determining which court has authority over a case.
• **Remedies** – Monetary damages, injunctions, specific performance, restitution. | | **Legal Institutions** | • **Courts** – Trial courts, appellate courts, supreme courts.
• **Law Enforcement** – Police, prosecutors (in some jurisdictions).
• **Regulatory Bodies** – Agencies overseeing specific sectors (e.g., securities regulators). | | **Legal Actors** | • **Plaintiff/Defendant** – Parties involved in the dispute.
• **Judges & Magistrates** – Adjudicators of civil cases.
• **Lawyers & Counselors** – Legal representation and advice.
• **Notaries & Mediators** – Facilitate documentation and alternative dispute resolution. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Good Faith & Fair Dealing** – Duty to act honestly in contractual relationships.
• **Equitable Remedies** – Courts may grant non-monetary relief when appropriate.
• **Presumption of Innocence** – Not applicable; civil cases rely on burden of proof ("preponderance of evidence"). | | **Specialized Subfields** | • **Intellectual Property** – Patents, trademarks, copyrights.
• **Consumer Protection** – Safeguarding buyers against unfair practices.
• **Environmental Law** – Regulations affecting property use and pollution. | These components interact to form a comprehensive system that resolves disputes, protects rights, and promotes fairness in private relations.
